name: Chicken
description: The default meat of all four cuisines.

unani.note: Murgh is garam — chicken soup for cold days.

histamine.note: Fresh/freshly-frozen is safe; leftovers and slow-cooked broths accumulate histamine fast.

name: Beef
description: Red meat staple, curries to burgers.

histamine.note: Freshness rules: freshly cooked fine; aged steak and ground beef sitting around are worse.

name: Lamb / mutton
description: The festival meat — and every tradition's warmest.

tcm.note: Yang rou is TCM's defining warming meat — winter hot pot.

unani.note: Classic garam — nihari and paya weather.

histamine.note: Fresh lamb is well tolerated; same freshness caveat as all meat.

name: Goat meat
description: Lean red meat of desi 'mutton' curries.

ayurveda.note: Notably gentler than lamb in classical texts.

unani.note: Milder garam than mutton/lamb.

histamine.note: Fresh is fine.

name: Pork
description: The staple meat of Chinese and Western kitchens.

tcm.note: Unusually for meat, TCM calls pork neutral-cool and yin-nourishing.

ayurveda.note: Heavy; thinly classified.

unani.note: Not consumed/classified in Unani practice.

histamine.note: Fresh is moderate; cured forms (bacon, ham, sausage) are a 3.

name: Duck
description: Rich dark poultry; Peking duck to salan.

tcm.note: The yin poultry — opposite of chicken.

ayurveda.note: Heavy-oily; thin documentation.

unani.note: Waterfowl generally garam-tar; sources vary.

histamine.note: Fresh fine; roasted-hung preparations age the meat.

name: Egg (chicken)
description: The universal breakfast protein.

unani.note: Anda is classically garam — half-boiled eggs for winter.

histamine.note: Raw/runny egg WHITE is the liberator; well-cooked eggs are fine for most.

name: White fish (fresh)
description: Mild white-fleshed fish, fried or curried.

ayurveda.note: Fish is classically ushna — the fish+milk incompatibility rule.

unani.note: Machli is garam — a winter food in desi logic.

histamine.note: THE safe protein — but only very fresh or frozen-at-sea; histamine forms within hours unrefrigerated.

name: Salmon
description: Rich pink oily fish.

ayurveda.note: As fish generally.

histamine.note: Fresh/frozen fine for many; SMOKED salmon is a 3.

name: Tuna (canned)
description: Pantry protein — and the textbook histamine hazard.

ayurveda.note: As fish.

histamine.note: Scombroid fish: histamine forms before canning — the classic 'fish poisoning' is a histamine event.

name: Sardines (canned)
description: Small oily canned fish.

histamine.note: Scombroid-class; canned small oily fish run very high.

name: Mackerel
description: Strong-flavored oily fish.

histamine.note: The namesake scombroid fish — spoils into histamine fastest of all.

name: Shrimp / prawns
description: Sweet shellfish of every coast.

unani.note: Jhinga is famously garam in desi usage.

histamine.note: Shellfish are liberators; freshness critical.

name: Crab
description: Sweet shellfish — famously 'cold' in Chinese food culture.

tcm.note: So cold it's traditionally eaten with warming ginger vinegar.

ayurveda.note: Shellfish heating per most; disagrees with TCM.

histamine.note: Shellfish liberator; eat very fresh.

name: Squid
description: Chewy cephalopod, grilled or fried.

ayurveda.note: As seafood generally; thin documentation.

histamine.note: Moderate; freshness critical as with all seafood.

name: Tofu
description: Fresh soybean curd.

unani.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: Fresh tofu is moderate; fermented tofu (furu) and aged forms are a 3.

name: Edamame
description: Young green soybeans in the pod.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: Milder than mature soy.

name: Chickpeas
description: The legume of chole, hummus, and besan.

ayurveda.note: Cooling-dry per texts — yet desi folk calls chana garam; both recorded.

unani.note: Nakhud is garam in Unani sources.

histamine.note: Legumes are mildly flagged; usually fine fresh-cooked.

name: Red lentils (masoor)
description: Fast-cooking everyday dal; shorbat adas.

ayurveda.note: Masoor is one of the warmer dals.

histamine.note: Fresh-cooked dal is fine for most; reheated day-old less so.

name: Brown/green lentils
description: Whole lentils of mujadara and soups.

ayurveda.note: Milder than split masoor.

unani.note: Adas is classically garam-yabis.

histamine.note: As legumes generally.

name: Mung beans
description: The gentlest dal — and TCM's classic heat-clearing bean.

tcm.note: Lu dou soup is THE TCM summer cooler and detoxifier.

ayurveda.note: The sattvic, tridoshic dal of khichdi.

histamine.note: Among the safest legumes fresh-cooked.

name: Urad dal (black gram)
description: Heavy creamy dal of dal makhani and dosa batter.

ayurveda.note: The heaviest, most heating dal — a strength-builder.

unani.note: Maash is textbook garam.

histamine.note: Fermented forms (dosa/idli batter) add histamine.

name: Kidney beans (rajma)
description: Red beans of rajma-chawal and chili.

ayurveda.note: Heavy, vata-forming; schools vary.

histamine.note: As legumes; canned versions slightly worse than home-cooked.

name: Black beans
description: Earthy beans; TCM's kidney-nourishing hei dou.

histamine.note: Fermented black beans (douchi) are a 3 — different food.

name: Black-eyed peas (lobia)
description: Quick-cooking spotted beans.

ayurveda.note: Lighter than most beans; schools vary.

histamine.note: As legumes.

name: Fava beans (ful)
description: The bean of Egypt's national breakfast.

ayurveda.note: Thinly classified.

unani.note: Baqilla leans cold-heavy in Unani texts — hence the warming cumin/oil dressing.

histamine.note: Histamine-modest — but causes favism in G6PD-deficient people (a separate, serious issue).

name: Soybeans
description: The mother bean of tofu, soy milk, and sauce.

ayurveda.note: Heavy; thinly classified.

histamine.note: Higher than other legumes; fermented soy products higher still.

name: Peanuts
description: The everyday roasted legume-nut.

unani.note: Moongphali is winter street food — classic garam.

histamine.note: Liberator — and a major true allergen besides.

name: Almonds
description: The prized nut of badam milk and Unani tonics.

ayurveda.note: Heating — but soaked & peeled becomes neutral-building, per classical rule.

unani.note: Badam is garam; sardai (soaked-ground) tempers it.

histamine.note: Among the better-tolerated nuts.

name: Walnuts
description: Brain-shaped nut; TCM's kidney-warming tonic.

unani.note: Akhrot is textbook garam — winter food.

histamine.note: One of the more histamine-problematic nuts.

name: Cashews
description: Creamy nut of korma pastes and snack tins.

histamine.note: Flagged alongside walnuts.

name: Pistachios
description: Green nut of kheer, kunafa, and baklava.

unani.note: Pista is garam in Unani texts.

histamine.note: Middling among nuts.

name: Pine nuts
description: Delicate nut of fatteh, pesto, and chilgoza winters.

unani.note: Chilgoza/snobar is a classic winter garam nut.

histamine.note: Usually fine; rancidity is the bigger issue.

name: Pumpkin seeds
description: Green flat seeds, roasted for snacking.

ayurveda.note: Mild; thinly classified.

unani.note: Seed used in cooling majoons by some hakims.

histamine.note: A histamine-safe snack seed.

name: Sunflower seeds
description: The cracking-snack seed of Chinese and Arab gatherings.

histamine.note: Mostly fine; rancid seeds worse.

name: Chia seeds
description: Gel-forming little seeds (often confused with desi sabja — see basil seeds).

ayurveda.note: Used like cooling sabja in modern practice; not classical.

unani.note: Treated like tukh malanga in modern desi use.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Flaxseed
description: Oily seed ground into winter pinnis and porridges.

ayurveda.note: Alsi is classically ushna — a winter laddu seed.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.
